model.saas_analytics.int_customer_month_.name: int_customer_month_mrr
model.saas_analytics.int_customer_month_.description:
Month-end subscription state and monthly recurring revenue (MRR) of every customer, one row per customer per month, from the customer's first month (the month of their `started` event) through the last month covered by the data. This is the base for the MRR metrics.
The state of a month is the latest subscription event strictly before the first instant of the following month. MRR is seats multiplied by the price per seat for the plan and billing interval (annual plans use the discounted price, already expressed per month), in cents. It is 0 when the state is `canceled`. A customer who is canceled keeps getting rows up to the last month, so churn is an explicit row with MRR 0, not a missing one. A `canceled` event still carries the plan and seats from before the cancellation, so activity must be read from `event_type`, never from `plan` or `seats`.
MRR here is a month-end snapshot of the subscription, not billed revenue: an annual customer's invoice covers twelve months, while their MRR is one twelfth of it each month. Changes that start and end inside one month do not appear: only the month-end state is kept. Assumption, not enforced: no two events of one customer share a timestamp. If they did, the choice of the event for that month would be arbitrary.

customer_id.name: customer_id
customer_id.description: Customer identifier. Together with `month` it forms the grain of this model.

month.name: month
month.description: First day of the calendar month whose end-of-month state this row describes. Together with `customer_id` it forms the grain of this model.

event_id.name: event_id
event_id.description: Identifier of the subscription event that defines the customer's state at the end of this month.

event_type.name: event_type
event_type.description: Type of the defining event. `started`, `plan_changed`, `seats_changed` and `reactivated` mean the customer is active at month end. `canceled` means the customer is inactive and has no MRR, although `plan` and `seats` still show the values from before the cancellation.

plan.name: plan
plan.description: Plan after the defining event (starter, pro or business). For a canceled customer, the last plan before the cancellation.

seats.name: seats
seats.description: Number of seats after the defining event. For a canceled customer, the seats before the cancellation.

billing_interval.name: billing_interval
billing_interval.description: Billing interval after the defining event (monthly or annual). Annual plans use the discounted per-seat price.

reason.name: reason
reason.description: Reason recorded on the defining event, when there is one: `upgrade` or `downgrade` for a plan change, `voluntary` or `payment_failed` for a cancellation. Empty for the other event types.

price_per_seat_month_cents.name: price_per_seat_month_cents
price_per_seat_month_cents.description: Price of one seat for one month, in cents, for the row's plan and billing interval (from the `plan_prices` seed). Filled in for canceled rows too, where it is informational only: the MRR of a canceled row is 0.

mrr_cents.name: mrr_cents
mrr_cents.description: Monthly recurring revenue of the customer at the end of the month, in cents: seats multiplied by `price_per_seat_month_cents`, or 0 when `event_type` is `canceled`. Summing it over customers gives the total MRR of the month.

model.saas_analytics.int_customer_month_.raw_code:
with cs_first_month as (
    select
        customer_id,
        date_trunc(event_ts, month) as first_month
    from
        {{ ref('stg_subscription_events') }}
    where
        event_type = 'started'
),

date_spine as (
    select month
    from
        unnest(generate_date_array(
            (
                select date_trunc(min(_batch_date), month) from {{ ref('stg_subscription_events') }}
            ),
            (
                select date_trunc(max(_batch_date), month) from {{ ref('stg_subscription_events') }}
            ),
            interval 1 month
        )) as month
),

customer_months as (
    select 
        cfm.customer_id, 
        ds.month
    from
        cs_first_month as cfm
    cross join 
        date_spine as ds
    where ds.month >= cfm.first_month
),

joined_subscription_events as (
    select
        cms.customer_id,
        cms.month,
        row_number() over(partition by cms.customer_id, cms.month order by event_ts desc) as month_row_num,
        se.event_id,
        se.event_type,
        se.event_ts,
        se.plan,
        se.seats,
        se.billing_interval,
        se.reason
    from 
        customer_months as cms
    left join 
        {{ ref('stg_subscription_events') }} as se
    on 
        cms.customer_id = se.customer_id and
        se.event_ts < date_add(cms.month, interval 1 month)
),

month_end_state as (
    select
        customer_id,
        month,
        event_id,
        event_type,
        plan,
        seats,
        billing_interval,
        reason
    from
        joined_subscription_events
    where
        month_row_num = 1
),

join_plan_prices as (
    select
        mes.customer_id,
        mes.month,
        mes.event_id,
        mes.event_type,
        mes.plan,
        mes.seats,
        mes.billing_interval,
        mes.reason,
        pp.price_per_seat_month_cents,
        case
            when mes.event_type <> 'canceled' then mes.seats * pp.price_per_seat_month_cents
            else 0
        end as mrr_cents
    from
        month_end_state as mes
    left join
        {{ ref('plan_prices') }} as pp 
        on mes.plan = pp.plan and
        mes.billing_interval = pp.billing_interval

)

select * from join_plan_prices

model.saas_analytics.int_customer_mrr_mo.name: int_customer_mrr_movements
model.saas_analytics.int_customer_mrr_mo.description:
Month-over-month MRR movement of every customer, one row per customer per month, with the same rows as `int_customer_month_mrr` (from each customer's first month through the last month in the data). It compares each month's MRR with the previous month's and classifies the change, so that the monthly bridge, retention and cohort models can aggregate it without repeating the logic.
Movement types, decided only from MRR and MRR history, never from event types: `new` (previous MRR is 0, MRR is above 0, and the customer never had MRR at an earlier month end), `reactivation` (the same, but the customer had MRR at some earlier month end), `expansion` (MRR rose and was already above 0), `contraction` (MRR fell but is still above 0), `churn` (previous MRR above 0, MRR is 0), and `nothing` (no change, including 0 to 0). A customer who starts and cancels inside one month never has month-end MRR, so their later return counts as `new`.
The amount is signed: positive for new, reactivation and expansion; negative for contraction and churn. For every row, `last_month_mrr_cents + movement_amount_cents = mrr_cents`. The monthly bridge model must flip the sign of contraction and churn to report them as positive numbers. All amounts are in cents.

customer_id.name: customer_id
customer_id.description: Customer identifier. Together with `month` it forms the grain of this model.

month.name: month
month.description: First day of the calendar month. The MRR on this row is the month-end value.

event_type.name: event_type
event_type.description: Type of the subscription event that defines the customer's state at the end of this month (started, plan_changed, seats_changed, canceled or reactivated). It describes the state, not the movement: it keeps its value in months where nothing changed.

plan.name: plan
plan.description: Plan at month end. For a canceled customer, the last plan before the cancellation.

seats.name: seats
seats.description: Number of seats at month end. For a canceled customer, the seats before the cancellation.

billing_interval.name: billing_interval
billing_interval.description: Billing interval at month end (monthly or annual).

price_per_seat_month_cents.name: price_per_seat_month_cents
price_per_seat_month_cents.description: Price of one seat for one month, in cents, for the row's plan and billing interval. Informational on canceled rows, where MRR is 0.

mrr_cents.name: mrr_cents
mrr_cents.description: Monthly recurring revenue of the customer at the end of this month, in cents. 0 when the customer is canceled.

last_month_mrr_cents.name: last_month_mrr_cents
last_month_mrr_cents.description: MRR of the same customer at the end of the previous month, in cents. 0 for the customer's first month.

reason.name: reason
reason.description: Reason recorded on the defining event: `upgrade` or `downgrade` for a plan change, `voluntary` or `payment_failed` for a cancellation. Empty for other event types. Used to split churn into voluntary and involuntary.

movement_type.name: movement_type
movement_type.description: Kind of MRR movement in this month: new, reactivation, expansion, contraction, churn or nothing. Defined in the model description.

max_history_amount_cents.name: max_history_amount_cents
max_history_amount_cents.description: Highest month-end MRR the customer had in any earlier month, in cents; 0 if there is no earlier month or no earlier month with MRR. Above 0 means the customer was active before, which separates `reactivation` from `new`.

movement_amount_cents.name: movement_amount_cents
movement_amount_cents.description: Signed change in MRR caused by the movement, in cents: positive for new, reactivation and expansion, negative for contraction and churn, 0 for nothing.

model.saas_analytics.int_customer_mrr_mo.raw_code:
with last_month_mrr as (
    select
        customer_id,
        month,
        event_type,
        plan,
        seats,
        billing_interval,
        reason,
        price_per_seat_month_cents,
        mrr_cents,
        ifnull(
            lag(mrr_cents) over (partition by customer_id order by month), 0
        ) as last_month_mrr_cents,
        ifnull(max(mrr_cents)
                    over (
                        partition by customer_id
                        order by month
                        rows between unbounded preceding and 1 preceding
                    ), 0) as max_history_amount_cents
    from {{ ref('int_customer_month_mrr') }}
),

movement_type_col as (
    select
        customer_id,
        month,
        event_type,
        plan,
        seats,
        billing_interval,
        reason,
        price_per_seat_month_cents,
        mrr_cents,
        last_month_mrr_cents,
        max_history_amount_cents,
        case
            when
                last_month_mrr_cents = 0
                and mrr_cents > 0
                and max_history_amount_cents = 0
                then 'new'
            when
                last_month_mrr_cents = 0
                and mrr_cents > 0
                and max_history_amount_cents > 0
                then 'reactivation'
            when mrr_cents > last_month_mrr_cents and mrr_cents > 0
                then 'expansion'
            when mrr_cents < last_month_mrr_cents and mrr_cents > 0
                then 'contraction'
            when last_month_mrr_cents > 0 and mrr_cents = 0
                then 'churn'
            else 'nothing'
        end as movement_type
    from
        last_month_mrr
),

amount_col as (
    select
        customer_id,
        month,
        event_type,
        plan,
        seats,
        billing_interval,
        price_per_seat_month_cents,
        mrr_cents,
        last_month_mrr_cents,
        reason,
        movement_type,
        max_history_amount_cents,
        case
            when
                (movement_type = 'new' or movement_type = 'reactivation')
                then mrr_cents
            when
                (movement_type = 'expansion' or movement_type = 'contraction')
                then mrr_cents - last_month_mrr_cents
            when movement_type = 'churn' then -last_month_mrr_cents
            else 0
        end as movement_amount_cents
    from
        movement_type_col
)

select * from amount_col

model.saas_analytics.mrr_monthly.name: mrr_monthly
model.saas_analytics.mrr_monthly.description:
Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) bridge, one row per calendar month: how total MRR moves from the end of the previous month to the end of this one. Built by summing `int_customer_mrr_movements`. Synthetic data (seed 42).
MRR is a month-end snapshot of subscriptions, not billed revenue. A customer's MRR is seats multiplied by the price per seat for their plan and billing interval (annual plans use the discounted price, already expressed per month), and 0 once they are canceled. Changes that start and end inside one month do not appear.
The bridge identity holds in every row: `starting_mrr + new_mrr + reactivation_mrr + expansion_mrr - contraction_mrr - churned_mrr = ending_mrr`. `starting_mrr` is the previous month's `ending_mrr` (0 in the first month). All amounts are in cents, and all movement columns are reported as positive numbers; contraction and churn are subtracted in the identity.
Definitions: `new` is the first month in which a customer has MRR at a month end, so a customer who starts and cancels inside one month and returns later counts as new on their return. `reactivation` is a return of a customer who had MRR at an earlier month end. `expansion` and `contraction` are increases and decreases of a customer who stays active. `churn` is a customer going from MRR above 0 to 0.

month.name: month
month.description: First day of the calendar month. All figures describe the month-end state and the movements of that month.

starting_mrr.name: starting_mrr
starting_mrr.description: Total MRR at the end of the previous month, in cents. Equals the previous row's `ending_mrr`; 0 in the first month.

new_mrr.name: new_mrr
new_mrr.description: MRR added by customers who have month-end MRR for the first time, in cents.

reactivation_mrr.name: reactivation_mrr
reactivation_mrr.description: MRR added by returning customers who had MRR at an earlier month end but none at the previous month end, in cents.

expansion_mrr.name: expansion_mrr
expansion_mrr.description: MRR added by customers who were already active and now pay more (more seats or a higher plan), in cents.

contraction_mrr.name: contraction_mrr
contraction_mrr.description: MRR lost by customers who remain active but now pay less, in cents. Reported as a positive number and subtracted in the bridge.

churned_mrr.name: churned_mrr
churned_mrr.description: MRR lost by customers who were active at the previous month end and have no MRR now, in cents. Reported as a positive number and subtracted in the bridge.

ending_mrr.name: ending_mrr
ending_mrr.description: Total MRR of all customers at the end of the month, in cents.

active_customers.name: active_customers
active_customers.description: Number of customers with MRR above 0 at the end of the month.

new_customers.name: new_customers
new_customers.description: Number of customers counted as new in the month (not reactivations).

churned_customers.name: churned_customers
churned_customers.description: Number of customers who churned in the month: active at the previous month end, no MRR at this month end.

model.saas_analytics.mrr_monthly.raw_code:
with mrr_sums_by_type as (
    select
        month,
        ifnull(lag(sum(mrr_cents)) over (order by month), 0) as starting_mrr,
        sum(
            case
                when movement_type = 'new'
                    then movement_amount_cents
                else 0
            end
        ) as new_mrr,
        sum(
            case
                when movement_type = 'reactivation'
                    then movement_amount_cents
                else 0
            end
        ) as reactivation_mrr,
        sum(
            case
                when movement_type = 'expansion'
                    then movement_amount_cents
                else 0
            end
        ) as expansion_mrr,
        -sum(
            case
                when movement_type = 'contraction'
                    then movement_amount_cents
                else 0
            end
        ) as contraction_mrr,
        -sum(
            case
                when movement_type = 'churn'
                    then movement_amount_cents
                else 0
            end
        ) as churned_mrr,
        sum(mrr_cents) as ending_mrr,
        countif(mrr_cents > 0) as active_customers,
        countif(movement_type = 'new') as new_customers,
        countif(movement_type = 'churn') as churned_customers
    from {{ ref('int_customer_mrr_movements') }}
    group by month
)

select * from mrr_sums_by_type

model.saas_analytics.stg_customers.description: One row per customer, taken from the nightly customers dump. The dump is a snapshot of current state that is replaced on every load, so this model shows each customer as of the latest load and holds no history. Plan and seat changes over time are tracked in the snapshot and in stg_subscription_events. Synthetic data.

customer_id.description: Unique customer identifier, format cus_ followed by six digits (primary key).

company_name.name: company_name
company_name.description: Name of the customer company. Generated, not a real company.

country.name: country
country.description: Two-letter ISO country code of the customer.

signup_date.name: signup_date
signup_date.description: Date the customer first started a subscription. Not changed by cancellation or reactivation.

plan.name: plan
plan.description: Current plan (starter, pro or business). For canceled customers, the plan held at cancellation.

seats.name: seats
seats.description: Current number of paid seats. For canceled customers, the seats held at cancellation.

billing_interval.name: billing_interval
billing_interval.description: How the customer is billed: monthly, or annual with a 20 percent discount. A reactivated customer returns on monthly billing.

status.name: status
status.description: active or canceled. Canceled covers both voluntary cancellation and cancellation after repeated payment failure.

_batch_date.name: _batch_date
_batch_date.description: Date of the dump this row came from. Identical for every row, because the raw table is replaced on each load.

model.saas_analytics.stg_invoices.name: stg_invoices
model.saas_analytics.stg_invoices.description: One row per invoice issued. An invoice is created when a subscription starts, at every renewal (monthly or annual) and when a customer reactivates. An invoice says what was billed, not whether it was paid: payment outcomes are in stg_payment_attempts. Annual invoices cover 12 months, so amount_cents is not monthly recurring revenue and must not be summed as MRR.

invoice_id.name: invoice_id
invoice_id.description: Unique identifier of the invoice (primary key).

plan.name: plan
plan.description: Plan billed on this invoice (starter, pro or business), as it was at issue time.

seats.name: seats
seats.description: Number of seats billed, as it was at issue time.

billing_interval.name: billing_interval
billing_interval.description: Period this invoice covers: monthly (1 month) or annual (12 months, 20 percent discount on the per-seat price).

amount_cents.name: amount_cents
amount_cents.description: Total billed in cents: seats times the per-seat monthly price for the plan and interval, times the months covered. For example 1200 means 12.00 in currency.

currency.name: currency
currency.description: Currency of amount_cents. Always USD in this dataset.

_batch_date.name: _batch_date
_batch_date.description: Date of the daily batch that delivered this invoice.

source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.customers.name: customers
source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.customers.description: One row per customer. A dump of the customers table as of the end of the loaded day, replaced in full on every load, so it holds current state only and no history. It is the source for the dbt snapshot.

_batch_date.name: _batch_date
_batch_date.description: Date of the dump. The same value on every row, because the table is replaced on each load.

source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.customers.source_description: Raw tables for the SaaS subscription analytics project. SYNTHETIC data produced by a seeded generator (generate_saas_data.py, seed 42), not from a real company. Loaded into BigQuery by load_to_bq.py in daily batches. Raw means untouched: every column is a STRING except _batch_date (DATE), and nothing is deduplicated, filtered or corrected. Cleaning happens in the staging models.

source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.invoices.name: invoices
source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.invoices.description: One row per invoice issued. Append-only: each daily batch adds the invoices issued that day. Records what was billed, not whether it was paid.

_batch_date.name: _batch_date
_batch_date.description: Date of the daily batch that delivered the row.

Raw means untouched: every column is a STRING except _batch_date (DATE), and nothing is deduplicated, filtered or corrected. Cleaning happens in the staging models.

source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.payment_a.name: payment_attempts
source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.payment_a.description: One row per attempt to charge an invoice, including failed attempts and retries. Append-only: each daily batch adds the attempts made that day.

_batch_date.name: _batch_date
_batch_date.description: Date of the daily batch that delivered the row.

Raw means untouched: every column is a STRING except _batch_date (DATE), and nothing is deduplicated, filtered or corrected. Cleaning happens in the staging models.

source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.product_e.name: product_events
source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.product_e.description: One row per product usage event as delivered. Append-only, and delivery is at least once, so known quirks are present: some event_ids appear in more than one batch (duplicates), some events arrive 1 to 5 days after they happened (event_ts is earlier than _batch_date), and about 0.1 percent reference a customer_id that does not exist in customers. All are left as delivered and handled in staging.

event_ts.name: event_ts
event_ts.description: Time the event happened. No time zone in the source.

_batch_date.name: _batch_date
_batch_date.description: Date of the daily batch that delivered the row. Later than the date of event_ts for late events.

source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.subscript.name: subscription_events

Each row carries the full state after the change. A few events are delivered twice; the copy is left as delivered and removed in staging.

event_ts.name: event_ts
event_ts.description: Time the change happened. No time zone in the source.

_batch_date.name: _batch_date
_batch_date.description: Date of the daily batch that delivered the row.

source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.truth_mrr.name: truth_mrr_monthly
source.saas_analytics.raw_saas.truth_mrr.description: Ground truth produced by the data generator (seed 42): the true monthly MRR bridge, one row per month. Computed by an independent replay of the generator's own state, not by the dbt models. Used only by the reconciliation tests; it is not production data.

month.name: month
month.description: Calendar month as text in `YYYY-MM` format (not a date). Convert before comparing with model months.

starting_mrr.name: starting_mrr
starting_mrr.description: Total MRR at the end of the previous month, in cents. 0 in the first month.

new_mrr.name: new_mrr
new_mrr.description: MRR added by customers with month-end MRR for the first time, in cents.

reactivation_mrr.name: reactivation_mrr
reactivation_mrr.description: MRR added by returning customers who had MRR at an earlier month end, in cents.

expansion_mrr.name: expansion_mrr
expansion_mrr.description: MRR added by active customers who now pay more, in cents.

contraction_mrr.name: contraction_mrr
contraction_mrr.description: MRR lost by customers who stay active but now pay less, in cents. Stored as a positive number.

churned_mrr.name: churned_mrr
churned_mrr.description: MRR lost by customers who went from active to no MRR, in cents. Stored as a positive number.

ending_mrr.name: ending_mrr
ending_mrr.description: Total MRR at the end of the month, in cents.

active_customers.name: active_customers
active_customers.description: Number of customers with MRR above 0 at the end of the month.

new_customers.name: new_customers
new_customers.description: Number of customers counted as new in the month (not reactivations).

churned_customers.name: churned_customers
churned_customers.description: Number of customers who churned in the month.

nrr_monthly.name: nrr_monthly
nrr_monthly.description: Monthly net revenue retention: MRR now of last month's customers divided by their MRR last month. Empty in the first month, where there is no previous month.

grr_monthly.name: grr_monthly
grr_monthly.description: Monthly gross revenue retention: like net retention, but each customer's MRR is capped at last month's value, so expansion is excluded. Empty in the first month.

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_column.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_column_stats_sql() %}
    select
        table_catalog,
        table_schema,
        shard_name,
        max(is_partitioning_column) = 1 as is_partitioned,
        max(partition_column) as partition_column,
        max(is_clustering_column) = 1 as is_clustered,
        array_to_string(
            array_agg(
                cluster_column ignore nulls
                order by clustering_ordinal_position
            ), ', '
        ) as clustering_columns
    from columns
    group by 1, 2, 3

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_column.name: _bigquery__get_columns_sql
macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_column.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_columns_sql(db_schema) %}
    select
        columns.table_catalog,
        columns.table_schema,
        columns.table_name as shard_name,
        coalesce(paths.field_path, '<unknown>') as column_name,
        -- invent a row number to account for nested fields
        -- BQ does not treat these nested properties as independent fields
        row_number() over (
            partition by
                columns.table_catalog,
                columns.table_schema,
                columns.table_name
            order by
                columns.ordinal_position,
                paths.field_path
        ) as column_index,
        coalesce(paths.data_type, '<unknown>') as column_type,
        paths.description as column_comment,
        case when columns.is_partitioning_column = 'YES' then 1 else 0 end as is_partitioning_column,
        case when columns.is_partitioning_column = 'YES' then paths.field_path end as partition_column,
        case when columns.clustering_ordinal_position is not null then 1 else 0 end as is_clustering_column,
        case when columns.clustering_ordinal_position is not null then paths.field_path end as cluster_column,
        columns.clustering_ordinal_position
    {# DIVERGENCE BEGIN #}
    from `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS columns
    join `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMN_FIELD_PATHS paths
    {# DIVERGENCE END #}
        on paths.table_catalog = columns.table_catalog
        and paths.table_schema = columns.table_schema
        and paths.table_name = columns.table_name
        and paths.column_name = columns.column_name
    where columns.ordinal_position is not null
{% endmacro %}

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_extend.name: _bigquery__get_extended_catalog_sql
macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_extend.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_extended_catalog_sql() %}
    select
        tables.table_catalog as table_database,
        tables.table_schema,
        case
            when tables.is_date_shard then concat(tables.table_name, '*')
            else tables.table_name
        end as table_name,
        tables.table_type,
        tables.table_comment,
        -- coalesce column metadata fields to ensure they are non-null for catalog generation
        -- external table columns are not present in COLUMN_FIELD_PATHS
        coalesce(columns.column_name, '<unknown>') as column_name,
        coalesce(columns.column_index, 1) as column_index,
        coalesce(columns.column_type, '<unknown>') as column_type,
        coalesce(columns.column_comment, '') as column_comment,

        'Shard count' as `stats__date_shards__label`,
        table_stats.shard_count as `stats__date_shards__value`,
        'The number of date shards in this table' as `stats__date_shards__description`,
        tables.is_date_shard as `stats__date_shards__include`,

        'Shard (min)' as `stats__date_shard_min__label`,
        table_stats.shard_min as `stats__date_shard_min__value`,
        'The first date shard in this table' as `stats__date_shard_min__description`,
        tables.is_date_shard as `stats__date_shard_min__include`,

        'Shard (max)' as `stats__date_shard_max__label`,

        'The last date shard in this table' as `stats__date_shard_max__description`,
        tables.is_date_shard as `stats__date_shard_max__include`,

        '# Rows' as `stats__num_rows__label`,
        table_stats.row_count as `stats__num_rows__value`,
        'Approximate count of rows in this table' as `stats__num_rows__description`,
        tables.is_table as `stats__num_rows__include`,

        'Approximate Size' as `stats__num_bytes__label`,
        table_stats.size_bytes as `stats__num_bytes__value`,
        'Approximate size of table as reported by BigQuery' as `stats__num_bytes__description`,
        tables.is_table as `stats__num_bytes__include`,

        'Partitioned By' as `stats__partitioning_type__label`,
        column_stats.partition_column as `stats__partitioning_type__value`,
        'The partitioning column for this table' as `stats__partitioning_type__description`,
        column_stats.is_partitioned as `stats__partitioning_type__include`,

        'Clustered By' as `stats__clustering_fields__label`,
        column_stats.clustering_columns as `stats__clustering_fields__value`,
        'The clustering columns for this table' as `stats__clustering_fields__description`,
        column_stats.is_clustered as `stats__clustering_fields__include`

    from tables
    join table_stats
        on table_stats.table_catalog = tables.table_catalog
        and table_stats.table_schema = tables.table_schema
        and table_stats.table_name = tables.table_name
    left join column_stats
        on column_stats.table_catalog = tables.table_catalog
        and column_stats.table_schema = tables.table_schema
        and column_stats.shard_name = table_stats.latest_shard_name
    left join columns
        on columns.table_catalog = tables.table_catalog
        and columns.table_schema = tables.table_schema
        and columns.shard_name = table_stats.latest_shard_name
{% endmacro %}

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_table_.name: _bigquery__get_table_shards_sql
macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_table_.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_table_shards_sql(db_schema) %}
    {% set region = "region-%s"|format(db_schema.identifier)%}
    select
        info_tables.table_catalog as table_catalog,
        info_tables.table_schema as table_schema,
        coalesce(REGEXP_EXTRACT(info_tables.table_name, '^(.+)[0-9]{8}$'), info_tables.table_name) as table_name,
        info_tables.table_name as shard_name,
        REGEXP_EXTRACT(info_tables.table_name, '^.+([0-9]{8})$') as shard_index,
        REGEXP_CONTAINS(info_tables.table_name, '^.+[0-9]{8}$') and  info_tables.table_type = 'BASE TABLE' as is_date_shard,
        info_tables.table_type as table_type,
        info_tables.table_type = 'BASE TABLE' as is_table,
        JSON_VALUE(table_description.option_value) as table_comment,
        table_storage.total_logical_bytes as size_bytes,
        table_storage.total_rows as row_count
    from `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES info_tables
    left join `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.MATERIALIZED_VIEWS materialized_views
        on materialized_views.table_catalog = info_tables.table_catalog
        and materialized_views.table_schema = info_tables.table_schema
        and materialized_views.table_name = info_tables.table_name
    left join `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_OPTIONS table_description
        on table_description.table_catalog = info_tables.table_catalog
        and table_description.table_schema = info_tables.table_schema
        and table_description.table_name = info_tables.table_name
        and table_description.option_name = 'description'
    left join `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ region }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_STORAGE table_storage
        on table_storage.table_catalog = info_tables.table_catalog
        and table_storage.table_schema = info_tables.table_schema
        and table_storage.table_name = info_tables.table_name
{% endmacro %}

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_table_.name: _bigquery__get_table_stats_sql
macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_table_.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_table_stats_sql() %}
    select
        table_catalog,
        table_schema,
        table_name,
        max(shard_name) as latest_shard_name,
        min(shard_index) as shard_min,
        max(shard_index) as shard_max,
        count(shard_index) as shard_count,
        sum(size_bytes) as size_bytes,
        sum(row_count) as row_count
    from table_shards
    group by 1, 2, 3
{% endmacro %}

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_tables.name: _bigquery__get_tables_sql
macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_tables.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_tables_sql() %}
    select distinct
        table_catalog,
        table_schema,
        table_name,
        is_date_shard,
        table_type,
        is_table,
        table_comment
    from table_shards
{% endmacro %}

### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand` button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build, or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
